title: Machine learning designs bulk metallic glasses with peak hardness near 2,450 HV
summary: VIBANN used a dataset of 673 bulk metallic-glass compositions to guide the design of five alloys, synthesized as amorphous 2 mm rods. The paper's experimental results identify alloy A1, B68Nb24Fe4W4, as the hardest: 2,447 +/- 44 HV at a 0.5 N indentation load, with six replicate indentations. Hardness decreases with increasing load; the peak is not a value for every alloy or test condition. X-ray scattering and molecular dynamics support a structural interpretation within the studied composition range. The date refers to the May 2026 paper, rather than the institute's later August announcement.
organization: Max Planck Institute for Sustainable Materials

evidence.tested: Designed bulk metallic glasses reached a Vickers hardness of about 2450 HV, compared with other alloys under comparable conditions.
evidence.unknown: Discovery is constrained by the vastness of composition space and scarce validated data, and results apply under limited-data conditions.
evidence.ai_role: An uncertainty-aware latent-representation framework searched compositions, screened by chemical plausibility, novelty and predictive uncertainty.
